the presence of SMRs is associated with a better outcome in patients with acute myocardiac infarction, and is related with a higher rate of thrombectomy.

The main takeaway from our work is that

SMR is an important determinant of procedural success and is associated with better prognosis, and its relationship with thrombus anatomy could help to identify patients in need of thrombus aspiration in order to achieve better reperfusion and lower mortality.
